item.title: Sensory precision in food writing
item.description: Practise choosing precise terms for flavour, aroma, texture and mouthfeel in food and drink criticism. Distinguish neutral descriptions from praise and criticism, and notice where the balance of a dish determines the judgement.

children.definition: Producing a dry, puckering sensation in the mouth.
children.example: The quince skin was astringent enough to make my mouth pucker, even with a spoonful of custard.
children.translation_uz: ogʻizda quruqlik va tortishish hissini uygʻotadigan

children.definition: So sweet that it becomes unpleasant to eat or drink.
children.example: The buttercream was already cloying by the second bite, and the candied petals only made matters worse.

children.definition: Rich and smooth in the mouth, with a pleasantly fatty or silky texture.
children.example: The braised pork belly was unctuous, and a spoonful of pickled mustard greens cut through its richness.
children.translation_uz: ogʻizda yoqimli yogʻlilik va mayinlik hissini beradigan

children.definition: Having a pleasantly sharp, lively flavour, often from spice or acidity.
children.example: A piquant relish of green chilli and lime brought the grilled aubergine to life.

children.definition: Having a green aroma or flavour reminiscent of fresh herbs or grass.
children.example: The olive oil had a herbaceous aroma that reminded me of freshly cut grass.
children.translation_uz: hidi yoki taʼmi yangi koʻkat yoki yangi oʻrilgan oʻtni eslatadigan

children.definition: Having a pronounced drying grip on the palate from tannins, especially in wine.
children.example: The young red was tannic on its own, but the grip softened with a bite of lamb.

children.definition: Having a salty taste or smell reminiscent of seawater or a saltwater solution.
children.example: The oyster's briny liquor made the squeeze of lemon almost superfluous.
children.translation_ru: со вкусом или запахом морской воды или рассола
children.translation_uz: taʼmi yoki hidi dengiz suvi yoki namakobni eslatadigan

children.definition: Having the strong, distinctive flavour or smell associated with the meat of wild animals.
children.example: The venison pie had a gamey depth that held its own against the juniper in the gravy.
children.translation_ru: с характерным вкусом или запахом дичи
children.translation_uz: yovvoyi hayvon goʻshtiga xos taʼm yoki hidga ega

children.definition: Having an aroma or flavour reminiscent of tree resin, often with a pine-like or woody quality.
children.example: The mastic ice cream left a delicate resinous note that lingered after the sweetness faded.
children.translation_uz: hidi yoki taʼmi daraxt smolasini eslatadigan

children.definition: Having a harsh, irritating smell or taste, often like that of burnt food or smoke.
children.example: The blackened garlic gave the broth an acrid edge that overwhelmed the mushrooms.

children.definition: Having a dry, grainy texture that breaks down into fine particles when chewed.
children.example: The pear looked ripe, but its mealy flesh crumbled instead of yielding a mouthful of juice.

children.definition: Having a soft, thick consistency that wobbles or yields like jelly.
children.example: The chilled consommé was lightly gelatinous and melted as soon as it touched the tongue.

children.definition: Giving off small bubbles of gas that create a tingling sensation when drunk.
children.example: The cider was gently effervescent, with a fine prickle that faded before the apple flavour did.
children.translation_ru: с мелкими пузырьками газа, слегка пощипывающими язык

children.definition: Browned by heating sugars until they develop the flavour of caramel.
children.example: The tart had a thin crust of caramelized sugar that tasted of toffee.
